subject.title: [Refactor] Consolidate synthetic log formats across MCP service pipelines

question: Should the generic OpenClaw tools server and the Codex compatibility MCP adapter share a formal fatal-diagnostic format, or should their owner-specific prefixes remain independent?
rationale: Source confirms similar callbacks but no existing contract requiring identical output, and the two adapters cross a core-versus-Codex ownership boundary.

options.title: Keep Owner-Specific Diagnostics
options.body: Retain the current callbacks because shared transport is already centralized and no consumer contract requires identical stderr text.

options.title: Define A Shared Format
options.body: Introduce a small parameterized formatter beside the stdio helper, preserving each service name and adding focused tests for both entry points.

recommendation.title: Keep Owner-Specific Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Retain the current callbacks because shared transport is already centralized and no consumer contract requires identical stderr text.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent shared-stdio integration makes this contributor the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether another common abstraction belongs there.
